question: Can you do dhikr without wudu, in janabah or menses, or out of habit without full attention?
asked: She wants to maximize her dhikr and is trying to develop the habit of doing dhikr at all times. Can she make dhikr when she is not in wudu, in a state of menses, or in a state of janabah? And can she do dhikr while doing routine things like shopping or waiting for the bus, when she's not really paying attention? Is that good, permissible or sinful? Must you pay full attention when you do dhikr?
answer:
MashaAllah, tabarakAllah, it's a good question, and it's a question that shows the eagerness of our sister, that she wants to continuously do dhikr. And realize that Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala says in the Qur'an: "O you who believe, remember Allah frequently. Remember Allah frequently, and praise Him morning and evening." And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala also says in the Qur'an: "And those who remember Allah frequently," those men and women who remember Allah frequently. So Allah commands us in the Qur'an to remember Allah frequently, and we should try our best to remember Allah 'azza wa jall as much as possible.

And when a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "What do you advise me to do?", the Prophet ﷺ said, "Constantly move your tongue in the remembrance of Allah." In another hadith, an elderly man came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I am too weak to pray and fast like the rest of your young Sahaba, so tell me something that I can do to get to their level." And so the Prophet ﷺ held on to his tongue and said, "I command you to constantly do dhikr of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala." And the Hadith Qudsi famously remarks as well that Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala says: "I am as My servant thinks of Me. And if My servant thinks of Me in a gathering, then I will think of him in a gathering. And if My servant thinks of Me in himself, then I will think of him in Myself." And the hadith goes on. So the point being, the more that you do dhikr of Allah 'azza wa jall, the closer you will be to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala.

Now, your question was twofold. Number one: can I do dhikr in any state? The response is yes, by unanimous consensus, alhamdulillah; there is no controversy whatsoever. All of the scholars have said that you may do dhikr of Allah (SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Astaghfirullah, La ilaha illallah), which is not Qur'anic recitation. You may do dhikr of Allah and du'a to Allah in the state of wudu, and if you have broken your wudu, and if you are in the state of janabah, and if you are in the state of menses; it does not matter. **Dhikr of Allah can be done, and should be done, in every single state.**

And Allah mentions in the Qur'an: "They do dhikr of Allah standing, sitting and lying down." And the indication is that in every state you will do dhikr of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. And Aisha radiyAllahu 'anha remarked that the Prophet ﷺ would do dhikr of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala in each and every instance; in every state that he was in, he would do dhikr of Allah jalla jalaluhu. So you don't have to be in any particular state, or face any direction, or fulfill any preconditions. Dhikr can be done, and should be done, in each and every state.

Now, there's only one scenario in which it is discouraged to do dhikr, and that would be out loud when you're in the restroom. At that point in time it would not be appropriate, because it is not the place of doing dhikr with the tongue. But even then, it is permissible to remember Allah consciously in your head, and not physically with your tongue. 'Ikrimah, the famous student of the Sahaba, would not do dhikr of Allah with his tongue, but he said that when I'm in the restroom, I will do dhikr with my qalb: "wa lakin bi-qalbihi," he said. So the famous tabi'i remarked that when you're in the restroom, don't do dhikr with your tongue, but with your qalb. If a thought comes and you praise Allah for that thought, if you think of a blessing or whatever, you may think of something in your mind, and that's fine, but not with the tongue at that point in time.

Now, the second part of your question is: must I be in a state of consciousness, like khushu'? Because the Qur'an, as we know, should be recited in a state of khushu', and we should be paying attention as much as possible. And I have a longer Q&A about that; you could listen to that. As for dhikr, you do not need to be in a state of khushu'. It can be a habit, and you shall be rewarded for the habit. However, the degree of reward, and the efficiency and the quality of the reward, will be dependent upon the quality of your intention.

So you shall get rewarded if you are accustomed to doing dhikr in any state. You're in the shopping center and you're just used to saying, "SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah," and if you just say that, you will get ajr and reward for that habit, and Allah will bless you and barakah will come down. But there is no question that if you said "SubhanAllah" and it came from the heart, and you meant it, and you wanted to exalt Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, that takes it to a whole different level of reward and of khushu'. That's not the same as somebody who is simply habitually saying, "SubhanAllah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar." **And the one who says it habitually is far, far better than the one who never says it at all.**

So make it a habit, because that is the stepping stone to making it a habit with khushu'. Because it's levels, right? You're not going to get to the highest level immediately. So the first level is you train yourself to constantly do dhikr of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala; you train yourself to remember Allah wherever you are and to praise Allah. And the best praises that you can do are four: SubhanAllah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar. These are the four that you should ingratiate in your life. Make them part and parcel of every step you take, every breath if possible, every free moment that you have; just say these adhkar. If you want to add something, say, "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." And also start asking, "Astaghfirullah," and:

> رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ

Just make du'as, so that your whole day and your whole evening, when you're awake, is constantly full of dhikr. And this is one of the most powerful mechanisms to be saved from the punishment of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. Our Prophet ﷺ said in a hadith: "Nothing saves people more from Jahannam than the dhikr of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala." So that's a beautiful question, and I hope that, inshallah ta'ala, it has been answered.
